web.title: LPG traders call off strike after BERC promises to hear demands
web.description:
LPG traders have withdrawn their planned two-day shutdown after securing talks with the energy regulator over seven demands, including higher commissions and an end to alleged harassment.
The LP Gas Traders Cooperative Association scrapped the plan on Wednesday after talks with the chairman of the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC).
Association President Md Selim Khan told bdnews24.com the BERC chairman assured them at a 3pm meeting that their demands would be heard at a public hearing on Oct 29.
“In light of this, we are withdrawing the strike,” he said.
The association had earlier announced that all LPG shops across the country would remain closed on Oct 15 and 16.
At Monday’s press conference at the National Press Club, Selim warned that traders would close their shops indefinitely if their demands were not met within two days.

At a press conference after the meeting, the power minister warned that legal action would be taken against the traders concerned unless they withdrew the strike.
“If they do not withdraw the strike, the government will take legal action,” he said.
He said LPG is an essential commodity and attempts to press demands by disrupting its supply were unacceptable. He said action could be taken under the Essential Commodities Control Act of 1956.

“The government will not tolerate any attempt to use this as a pretext to hold the country hostage,” the commerce minister said.
After the ministers’ warnings, the association met the BERC chairman and scrapped the shutdown plan.
The association's key demand is that distributors' commission on each LPG cylinder be raised to Tk 150 or set at 7 percent of the retail price.

Among its other demands, the association said that once the BERC announces LPG prices for a month, any company seeking to change the price must do so through the commission.

The traders have also demanded that unused cylinders belonging to companies that have been unable to supply gas for a long period be refilled and released into the market.

web.title: LPG traders withdraw planned 15–16 Oct nationwide strike
web.description:
**Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) traders have called off their planned two-day nationwide strike scheduled for Thursday and Friday(15–16 October ).**
Selim Khan, president of the LPG Traders Cooperative Association, announced the decision on Wednesday following a high-level meeting at the Secretariat and the scheduling of a public hearing on LPG pricing for 29 October.
Earlier, Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku and Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir warned of stern legal action against traders if they proceeded with the planned nationwide suspension of LPG cylinder sales and distribution.
The warning came after the LPG distributors' platform announced on Monday (12 October ) a complete shutdown of LPG outlets across the country on 15 and 16 October to press home several demands.
Their demands include an end to alleged administrative harassment, a review of operators' commission rates and the release of thousands of unused gas cylinders into the domestic supply chain.
With the strike called off, traders are expected to raise their demands and pricing concerns at the public hearing scheduled for 29 October.

web.title: LPG traders withdraw nationwide strike after govt warning
web.description:
LPG traders have withdrawn their planned two-day nationwide strike following a warning from the government that legal action would be taken against anyone attempting to create an artificial crisis or halt market supply.
The decision to withdraw the strike was announced on Wednesday by LPG Gas Traders Co-operative Society Limited following a meeting with the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC).
Traders stepped back from their programme after receiving assurances that a public hearing regarding their seven-point demands would be held at BERC on 29 October.
Taher Quraishi, treasurer of the society, told TIMES that their next course of action would be decided after observing the outcome of the public hearing.
Earlier on Monday, the society had announced at a press conference at the National Press Club in Dhaka that LPG sales would be suspended across the country on Thursday and Friday.
Traders alleged that long-standing issues, including increasing distributor commissions, ensuring uninterrupted supply, and stopping administrative harassment, remained unresolved.
They had warned of launching a tougher movement after the two-day strike if these issues were not resolved.
On the morning before the strike was called off, Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, held a meeting with LPG importers at the Secretariat.
Speaking after the meeting, the energy minister said that repeated attempts to raise prices by disrupting commodity supply were [unacceptable](https://tob.news/govt-plans-long-term-lpg-supply-stability-warns-against-artificial-shortages/).
He warned that legal action would be taken against those involved if attempts were made to hold the public hostage by stopping LPG supply or to create market instability.

Among the demands of the traders, a key requirement is to increase the distributor commission per 12kg LPG cylinder from Tk50 to Tk150.
Their other demands include ensuring uninterrupted supply and stopping administrative harassment. BERC indicated that decisions on commission-related matters and other demands would be made through public hearing.

At the time the strike was announced, an LPG supply shortage was ongoing in various parts of the country. Cylinders were unavailable in many places, whilst in areas where they were found, they were being sold above the government-fixed price.
On 4 October, BERC increased the price of a 12kg cylinder by Tk252, fixing it at Tk1,837.
However, 12kg cylinders are being sold in the market for Tk2,100 to Tk2,500. Traders cited supply deficit as the cause of the crisis.

web.title: LPG traders call off nationwide strike
web.description:
LPG traders have withdrawn their announced two-day nationwide strike scheduled for 15 and 16 October.
Meanwhile, a public hearing on fixing liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices has been scheduled for 29 October.
LPG traders announced on Monday (12 October) that they would keep all LPG shops closed across the country on 15 and 16 October.
Earlier on Wednesday, the government warned of strict legal action if the traders did not withdraw the strike.
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir issued the warning at a joint press conference at the conference room of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources at the Secretariat in the morning.
